title: Deliver a true installable Android app experience (sideloadable) and improve app-name uniqueness configurability

requirements.text: Update the Android wrapper documentation to support a non–Play Store distribution flow (sideload), including clear steps to build a release APK/AAB, where to set the production canister URL, and how a user can install the APK on an Android device.

quotes: Though it may not be on play store, but please make it an app. I want an app.

acceptanceCriteria: `frontend/android-wrapper/README.md` contains an explicit section for sideload distribution (outside Play Store).
README includes the exact Gradle property to set for the production web URL (`nutriscan.baseUrl`) and an example value.
README includes steps to produce a release artifact (APK and/or AAB) using Android Studio and/or Gradle CLI.
README includes end-user installation steps for the generated APK (sideload), with any required device settings noted.

requirements.text: Fix Android wrapper branding consistency so the installed Android app shows the correct, unique user-facing app name and does not contain leftover internal naming (e.g., the current theme name reference). Ensure the Android wrapper builds successfully after the change.

quotes: So make it unique and Make it an app.

acceptanceCriteria: Android wrapper still builds (debug and release) with no resource/theme resolution errors.
The launcher label shown on Android uses the user-facing app name from `@string/app_name` (currently "Calorieshivam") in `frontend/android-wrapper/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`.
Any internal Android theme/style naming that still references an old app name (e.g., `Theme.Calorieman`) is updated to be consistent, and `AndroidManifest.xml` references the updated theme correctly.

requirements.text: Add a small in-web “Install App” entry point that explains (in English) how to get the Android app build (sideload) and what it is (a packaged version of the web app). This should reduce confusion for users who expect an app instead of a website.

quotes: Please make this an app. Website is very much Drainable. People will confuse

acceptanceCriteria: The web UI has a visible “Install App” link/button accessible to logged-out users (e.g., on the Login page) and/or logged-in users (e.g., in the header or settings/help area).

Clicking “Install App” opens a page/section/modal with concise English instructions for Android installation (sideload) and a pointer to where the APK comes from (repository build artifact / provided APK).
All user-facing text added for this feature is in English.

requirements.text: Make the user-facing app display name configurable from a single place for both the web app (header/login/tab title/alt text) and the Android wrapper (app_name string), so the owner can choose a more searchable unique name without hunting through multiple files.

quotes: Though my name is unique Kailash Shivam, but people may not be able to search it. So make it unique

acceptanceCriteria: There is one documented place to change the display name for the web app, and all existing UI locations update accordingly (header brand label, login title, image alt text, browser tab title).
There is one documented place to change the display name for the Android wrapper (`app_name`) and it is referenced consistently as the launcher label.

Documentation explicitly states that technical identifiers (e.g., Android package name `com.nutriscan.wrapper`, resource key `nutriscan_base_url`) must remain unchanged unless required for build correctness.

constraints: Do not modify files under `frontend/src/components/ui` (read-only UI components); compose them instead.
Keep all backend logic in the single Motoko actor (`backend/main.mo`); no new backend canisters/services.
Keep technical identifiers (e.g., Android package name, resource keys like `nutriscan_base_url`) unchanged unless strictly necessary for build correctness.
Use English for all user-facing text added or updated.
nonGoals: Publishing to the Google Play Store (the goal is an installable app experience even without Play Store).
Adding new backend features unrelated to packaging/branding/configurability.
